statements.label: supported

statements.label: supported

statements.note: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing found at least 41 modification sites, and AAGAA was the most frequent motif.

statements.label: supported

statements.note: Profiling of differentiating murine and human myoblasts identified conserved circRNAs regulated in myogenesis and altered in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The circ-ZNF609 open reading frame starts at the start codon shared with the linear transcript and ends at an in-frame stop codon generated by circularization.

statements.label: supported

statements.label: supported

statements.label: supported
statements.text: circHIPK3 binds miR-124 directly and reduces the activity of that miRNA.

statements.note: The abstract reports direct binding of circHIPK3 to miR-124 and inhibition of miR-124 activity.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: According to polysome profiling, computational prediction and mass spectrometry, hundreds of endogenous circRNAs have the potential to be translated in an m6A-driven way.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: m6A-driven circRNA translation needs eIF4G2 and YTHDF3, is boosted by METTL3/14, is reduced by FTO, and increases upon heat shock.

statements.note: The abstract calls m6A-driven initiation efficient but never compares it with cap-dependent translation of linear mRNAs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: circRNAs show enrichment of consensus m6A motifs, and translation initiation can be driven by just one m6A site.
statements.evidence: We discover that consensus m 6 A motifs are enriched in circRNAs and a single m 6 A site is sufficient to drive translation initiation.
statements.note: The abstract reports enrichment of consensus m6A motifs in circRNAs and that a single m6A site suffices to drive initiation.

statements.label: not_addressed

statements.text: Knocking down endogenous circ-Foxo3 increased cell proliferation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Circ-Foxo3 showed high expression in non-cancer cells and was linked to cell cycle progression.

statements.evidence: Ectopic expression of circ-Foxo3 repressed cell cycle progression by binding to the cell cycle proteins cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (also known as cell division protein kinase 2 or CDK2) and cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1 (or p21), resulting in the formation of a ternary complex.
statements.note: Ectopic circ-Foxo3 repressed cell cycle progression by binding CDK2 and p21 into a ternary complex.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Dinucleotides on either side of a target site had a 100-fold effect, and each miRNA had its own noncanonical target sites.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The affinity data supported a biochemical model of miRNA-mediated repression, which a convolutional neural network extended to every miRNA sequence.
statements.evidence: These data enabled construction of a biochemical model of miRNA-mediated repression, which was extended to all miRNA sequences using a convolutional neural network.
statements.note: The measured affinities enabled a biochemical repression model that a convolutional neural network extended to all miRNA sequences.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Using this biochemical model made predictions of repression in cells substantially better.
statements.evidence: This model substantially improved prediction of cellular repression

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Serum exosomes from normal mice, unlike those from ADicerKO mice, could mimic the gene regulation produced by adipose tissue transplantation.

statements.evidence: Here we show that mice with an adipose-tissue-specific knockout of the microRNA (miRNA)-processing enzyme Dicer (ADicerKO), as well as humans with lipodystrophy, exhibit a substantial decrease in levels of circulating exosomal miRNAs.
statements.note: Both ADicerKO mice and humans with lipodystrophy showed a substantial decrease in circulating exosomal miRNAs.

statements.label: supported

statements.note: The abstract describes this cross-mouse regulation of a 3' UTR reporter in the liver through serum exosomal transfer.

statements.label: supported

statements.evidence: Here we report that m(6)A-containing RNAs exhibit accelerated deadenylation that is mediated by the CCR4-NOT deadenylase complex.
statements.note: The abstract reports accelerated deadenylation of m6A-containing RNAs mediated by CCR4-NOT.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: YTHDF2 recruits CCR4-NOT through direct contact between its N-terminal region and the CNOT1 SH domain, which is essential for CAF1- and CCR4-mediated deadenylation of m6A-containing RNAs.
statements.evidence: YTHDF2 recruits the CCR4-NOT complex through a direct interaction between the YTHDF2 N-terminal region and the SH domain of the CNOT1 subunit, and that this recruitment is essential for the deadenylation of m(6)A-containing RNAs by CAF1 and CCR4

statements.label: not_addressed

statements.note: The abstract shows CCR4-NOT recruitment only for YTHDF2 and says nothing about whether other YTHDF family members do the same.

statements.label: not_addressed

statements.evidence: Notably, none of these effects requires the specific lncRNA transcripts themselves and instead involves general processes associated with their production, including enhancer-like activity of gene promoters, the process of transcription, and the splicing of the transcript.
statements.note: None of the effects required the specific lncRNA transcripts; they involved enhancer-like promoter activity, transcription and splicing.

statements.label: supported

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Leukemic cells with high FTO were more sensitive to R-2HG, whereas hyperactive MYC signalling gave resistance that MYC inhibition could reverse.
